app_exercised: Exercised FuelWell web app at http://localhost:3000 across 8+ routes including /app/dashboard, /app/log (mobile), /app/coach, /app/daily-review, /app/progress, /app/recipes, /app/settings, /app/meal-plan, and /preview. Interacted with meal search, keyboard navigation (5 tab-throughs), form inputs, touch targets (measured 171 interactive elements), color contrast analysis, and tested mobile responsiveness at 390x844 viewport. Captured screenshots and verified focus rings, button states, and microcopy consistency. Tested form flows including meal selection, portion controls, and navigation affordances.

findings.description: Search has no visible reset/clear button, forcing users to manually backspace or select-all to start a new search. For P01 logging in <10 seconds, this adds taps.
reproduction_steps: Navigate to http://localhost:3000/app/log on mobile (390px)
Type 'chicken' in the search input
Observe the search box — no X or Clear button is visible next to the input
findings.observed_evidence: Search input at /app/log shows placeholder 'Search 1,000+ foods by name' but no clearing affordance. Playwright test confirmed clearButton === null. Users must triple-click and delete or backspace through text.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an X button or clear icon inside the search input (right-aligned, 44x44px minimum) that appears when text is present. Use aria-label='Clear search' for accessibility.

findings.description: Multiple touch targets undersized on mobile meal log: filter pill buttons (All, Favorites, Dislikes, Recently used) measure 39-101px width but only 28px height, falling below 44px minimum.
reproduction_steps: Open http://localhost:3000/app/log on mobile viewport (390x844)
Examine the filter pills below the meal-type selector
Inspect 'All', 'Favorites', 'Dislikes', 'Recently used' buttons with browser dev tools
findings.observed_evidence: Touch target analysis via Playwright: button[39x28]='All', button[75x28]='Favorites', button[66x28]='Dislikes', button[101x28]='Recently used'. All are 28px tall (target: >=44px). Screenshot saved to A01-mobile-log-small-targets.png.
findings.suggested_fix: Increase filter pill height to 44px or larger. Alternatively, use a dropdown or segmented control that has adequate touch targets. Ensure 8px minimum padding around each tap zone.

findings.description: Unit notation is inconsistent across the app: meal-log page shows 39 occurrences of 'cal' (165 cal /100g) but only 2 'kcal'. This creates ambiguity in whether numbers are calories or kilocalories.
reproduction_steps: Navigate to http://localhost:3000/app/log
Search for any food item
Review the calorie notation on food results (e.g., 'Chicken breast, grilled 165 cal /100g')
Compare to dashboard where totals display as '850 kcal'
findings.observed_evidence: Text analysis from /app/log: 39 instances of 'cal', 2 instances of 'kcal', 86 instances of 'g' for grams. Dashboard shows '850/2250 kcal' and 'Nutrition2 meals logged' but food search shows '165 cal /100g'. No universal notation found.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize on one unit throughout the app. Recommend 'kcal' (kilocalories) with a consistent format like 'Amount: 165 kcal / 100g' in food search. Update all search results, nutritional displays, and dashboard to match.

findings.description: FuelWell logo and brand text has critically low contrast (1.49:1), failing WCAG AA standard (4.5:1 required). P02 relies on 150% zoom and high-contrast text; this branding element is essentially invisible to her.
reproduction_steps: Open http://localhost:3000/app/dashboard in browser
Inspect the logo/brand area at the top-left of the page
Measure color contrast between 'FuelWell' text and its background
findings.observed_evidence: Contrast analysis on /app/dashboard: Logo anchor element 'FuelWellDaily decision system' measured at 1.49:1 contrast ratio (outline: rgb(21, 145, 108) solid 2px on background). Additional 'FuelWell' span elements also 1.49:1. Screenshot: A01-desktop-dashboard-contrast.png. WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text.
findings.suggested_fix: Increase contrast of logo and brand text to at least 4.5:1 (7:1 preferred for AAA). Use darker text color on the current background, or lighten the background, or both. Test with 150% zoom and high-contrast OS settings.

findings.description: Meal section buttons (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, Snack) lack explicit role='button' attribute, relying only on aria-pressed. For P02 using accessibility features, semantic clarity helps.
reproduction_steps: Navigate to http://localhost:3000/app/log on mobile
Examine the buttons labeled 'Breakfast', 'Lunch', 'Dinner', 'Snack'
findings.observed_evidence: Playwright eval: Meal section buttons returned role=null but aria-pressed=true/false. HTML should include role='button' or use native <button> if not already. Standard semantic buttons improve screen reader and AT compatibility.
findings.suggested_fix: Ensure meal-type selector buttons have role='button' (or use native <button> element). Confirm aria-pressed is correctly toggled when selected. This clarifies intent for assistive tech users like P02.

findings.description: Number formatting at large zoom levels (150%+) may clip or overflow. No evidence of clipping on current test, but responsive text and padding need verification with actual zoom.
reproduction_steps: Open http://localhost:3000/app/dashboard at 150% browser zoom
Check macro numbers (e.g., '102g PROTEIN LEFT', '1400 CALORIES LEFT')
Verify no text truncation or overlap
findings.observed_evidence: Text truncation test at 390px width found no overflow. However, 150% zoom was not explicitly tested. Recommend manual verification with system zoom + 150% browser zoom together (P02's likely setup).
findings.suggested_fix: Test the dashboard, daily review, and progress pages at 150% zoom with reading glasses viewing distance. Ensure macro cards and stat displays remain readable without horizontal scroll. Use CSS breakpoints to reflow layouts if needed.

findings.description: Meal section buttons (Breakfast, Lunch, etc.) and filter pills use aria-pressed but do not explicitly signal which is selected through text or icon. Keyboard users benefit from both outline and indicator.
reproduction_steps: Open http://localhost:3000/app/log
Press Tab 5+ times to focus meal-type buttons
Observe visual focus ring and aria-pressed state — both should be independently clear
findings.observed_evidence: Keyboard focus test: Tab 1 lands on logo (outline visible), Tab 3-5 on menu items. Meal buttons show aria-pressed but no additional visual marker like underline or checkmark when selected. Focus rings present (oklab outline) but selection state is aria-only.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a visible underline, border-bottom, or checkmark icon to aria-pressed='true' buttons. This creates redundant (and thus more accessible) signaling for keyboard users and those with color-blindness.

findings.description: Send button on Coach page is disabled (aria-disabled state) but no tooltip or explanatory text clarifies why. P03 may assume it's a bug.
reproduction_steps: Navigate to http://localhost:3000/app/coach
Locate the 'Send' button at the bottom of the chat input
Note that it appears disabled (aria-disabled or disabled attribute present)
findings.observed_evidence: Coach page interactive elements list shows: button[48x48]='Send' DISABLED. No aria-label or title attribute indicates 'You must type a message first' or similar. P03 as a keyboard user will tab to this and wonder why it's greyed out.
findings.suggested_fix: Add aria-label='Send message (requires text input)' and/or a tooltip showing the requirement. Alternatively, enable the button and validate on focus/click to show an inline error.

findings.description: Daily review on mobile lacks a visible 'back' or 'collapse' button at the top of collapsed sections. P04 one-handed on a phone gets cognitively disoriented when sections auto-expand and has no quick way to retreat.
reproduction_steps: Open http://localhost:3000/app/daily-review on mobile (390x844)
Tap 'Ask coach' in the header section
Try to find a back or collapse button to return focus to the section header
findings.observed_evidence: Daily review mobile screenshot shows 'Collapse section' button but user may not see it after expanding into a coach input modal. No explicit 'Back' affordance visible in text output. P04 with interrupted attention needs a clear exit path.
findings.suggested_fix: Ensure 'Collapse section' or 'Back' button is always visible near the top of expanded sections, with clear visual hierarchy. Add a back arrow or 'X' button next to the section title. Test one-handed reach patterns on 6.1" phone.

findings.description: No loading skeleton or visual feedback during meal logging. P04 interrupted by baby may assume the app froze or lost her input if she doesn't see immediate response.
reproduction_steps: Navigate to http://localhost:3000/app/log on mobile
Search for 'chicken', click a result, select portion, and attempt to add to day
Observe whether a spinner, skeleton, or 'Saving...' message appears
findings.observed_evidence: Button state test found 2 add-related buttons but no aria-busy='true' states detected. No loading skeleton was mentioned in text output. Fast local app may mask this in production, but visual feedback is critical for cognitive-load users.
findings.suggested_fix: Add skeleton screens or spinner icons during: meal search (350ms+), portion selection update, and meal save. Use aria-busy='true' on the button during async operations. Provide haptic feedback (if mobile) or 'Added!' confirmation message.

findings.description: Daily review lacks a 'minimal mode' or 'glance-only' option for P04's use case (quick check if she's roughly on track). Current page shows many detailed sections that may overwhelm when tired.
reproduction_steps: Open http://localhost:3000/app/daily-review on mobile
Review the number of collapsible sections (Energy Ledger, Nutrition Detail, Fitness Detail, etc.)
Observe how much scrolling or expanding is needed to get the headline 'Am I on track?'
findings.observed_evidence: Daily review page has multiple collapsed sections. P04 needs a summary mode that shows only: today's total calories vs. target, protein vs. target, and a one-word sentiment (On track / Under / Over). Rest stays collapsed by default.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Summary view' toggle at the top of daily review. When on, show only the key metrics card and collapse all detail sections. Provide a one-tap way to switch to full view if she wants detail.

findings.description: Dark mode behavior not explicitly tested on /app/settings page. P04 uses night mode; ensure dark-mode colors meet contrast and do not introduce bright flashes.
reproduction_steps: Open http://localhost:3000/app/settings with dark-mode preference on mobile
Toggle any setting (e.g., goal, activity level)
Watch for white-background flashes or low-contrast text
findings.observed_evidence: Screenshot captured at dark mode: A01-mobile-settings-darkmode.png. Initial visual inspection shows expected dark theme. No bright flash or unthemed elements observed, but full dark-mode suite testing recommended.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify that all modals, tooltips, and form overlays respect dark mode color scheme. Test prefers-reduced-motion setting to ensure no animations flash or pulse in dark mode. Run through settings change flow in dim lighting.

findings.description: Portion input for meals uses min=0 but no validation message if user enters 0g. P01 logging fast may accidentally submit a 0g meal.
reproduction_steps: Navigate to http://localhost:3000/app/log on mobile
Search and select 'Chicken breast, grilled'
In the portion input, clear the value and type '0'
Attempt to add the meal
findings.observed_evidence: Portion input analysis: min=0, max='', step=''. No max validation visible. If user submits 0g, the meal would log with no macros (breaking the intent to track nutrition).
findings.suggested_fix: Either: (a) set min='1' on the input, or (b) show a validation error 'Portion must be greater than 0' on blur/submit. Add aria-describedby pointing to error text for accessibility.

findings.description: Favorite and dislike buttons on food search results may not provide immediate feedback (heart fill, color change, haptic) that P01's fast-paced workflow requires.
reproduction_steps: Open http://localhost:3000/app/log on mobile
Search 'chicken'
Click the heart icon or 'Like this' button on a result
Observe if the button changes color, fills, or provides tactile feedback
findings.observed_evidence: Food list shows button[44x44]='Like this' and button[44x44]='Not for me' on each result. No immediate visual change documented in output. Fast-logging users need instant confirmation that the preference was saved.
findings.suggested_fix: On click, animate the heart icon to fill/unfill with color, or change button background. Provide aria-live='polite' feedback: 'Added to favorites' or 'Removed from favorites'. Consider haptic vibration on mobile.

findings.description: Current nutrition data display uses abbreviations (p, c, f for protein/carbs/fat) in compact macro views. P02 with large-text settings or low vision may not immediately recognize these.
reproduction_steps: Open http://localhost:3000/app/dashboard
Look at the meal cards (e.g., 'Greek yogurt power bowl 330 cal 31g protein')
Examine the macro breakdown (31g pro, 40g carb, 7g fat)
findings.observed_evidence: Meal cards show abbreviated format: '31g pro, 40g carb, 7g fat'. P02 with 150% zoom and reading glasses may not parse 'pro' = protein or 'carb' = carbohydrate immediately.
findings.suggested_fix: In macro cards, use full text 'protein', 'carbs', 'fat' instead of abbreviations. If space is constrained on mobile, keep abbreviation but add aria-label='31g protein' for screen readers and tooltip on hover for visual clarity.

findings.description: Icons in the bottom nav (Home, Log, Coach, Move, Groceries, Review) lack visible labels on mobile, relying on icon alone. P02 may not immediately recognize them.
reproduction_steps: Open /app/dashboard on mobile (390x844)
Look at the bottom navigation bar
Examine whether each icon has a text label below it
findings.observed_evidence: Bottom nav shows icon-only buttons with aria labels: a[65x45]='Home', a[65x49]='Log', a[65x45]='Coach'. Text labels not visible in current layout. P02 with large text enabled may benefit from label visibility.
findings.suggested_fix: Show text labels below each bottom-nav icon (or next to on tablets). Ensure labels remain visible at 150% zoom. If space is tight, use a collapsed state on first load and expand on first interaction.
